units.translation: 1408. 〈And they quickly became dust and earth〉 [rushing]: through this he indicates how they became invisible.

1412-14. Whether heavenly: he says this because of the Nymphs, some are heavenly, some earthly, some river-dwelling, some of the marshes, some of the sea. And in general the race of Nymphs is divided into many kinds, as Mnesimachus of Phaselis says in his Diacosmi (fg 2 M. IV 453).
1415. ἐνωπαδίς: openly, in full view. Lᴳ P
1418. λωφήσομεν: instead of "we will cease." Properly, λωφῆσαι means to cast off a burden from the neck; for λόφος is the neck.
1421. εἰλαπίνας: here, sacrifices. Lᴳ (P)
1422. ἀδινῇ: weak, because of thirst. Lᵐ (P)
1433. κύντατος: the worst, the most shameful. Lᵐ P
1442a. παίφασσε: he groped, he was carried away in ecstasy. Lᵐ P
b. 〈παίφασσε:〉 he rushed. Sᵐ
1452. 〈περὶ〉 χηραμόν: around their own lair. Lᵐ (P)
1453a. γειομόροι: those who toil upon the earth. Lᵐ (P)
b. 〈ἠύτε μυῖαι:〉 upon the simile, another simile. Sᵐ
1454. λίβα: a drop. Lᴳ (P)
1460. δήοιμεν: we might find. Lᵐ P
1462. ἐπηλίνδητο: he was covered. Lᵐ Gᴳ P

1470. Eilatides Polyphemus: Polyphemus, left behind in Mysia, founded the city of Cius, which was named after the river flowing past it; fighting against the Chalybes he died, as Nymphodorus says (fg 18 M. II 380). That he founded Cius, Autocharis has said in the first book of his Chronicles (249 fg 1 J.).
1471. οὗ ἔθεν: instead of ἑαυτοῦ (his own). Lᴳ P
1487. αὐλείτης: the one from the farmstead, the rustic. The name is from αὖλιν (courtyard).
1490-94a. Λυκωρείοιο: instead of Delphic; for the Delphians were first called Lycoreans from a certain village Lycoreia.

b. βαρὺ κῦμα: instead of κύημα (swelling). Alexander in the first book of his Cretan History (fg 32 M. III 231) says that Hermes and Apollo had intercourse with Acacallis, and from Apollo was born Naxos, and from Hermes Cydon, after whom the city Cydonia in Crete is named.
c. Garamantes: a people of Libya.
d. 〈Γαράμαντα:〉 it is unclear whether the Garamantes in Libya were named after this Garamas or he after the people. There is also a temple among them, and Garamas is mentioned as a god.
